title: Non-renewable resources
competency: Distinguish between renewable and non-renewable natural resources.

keywords.def: Resources in limited supply that cannot be replaced once used.
Fuels such as coal, petroleum oil and natural gas, formed by natural processes over a very long time.
A precious gemstone that shows changing colours; a main export mineral of Ethiopia.

en.text: Non-renewable resources exist in limited supply and cannot be replaced once used. Examples are petroleum oil, natural gas, coal and other fossil fuels. Renewable resources can be used more than once and give lower carbon emission. Non-renewable ones can be used one time and give higher carbon emission.

screens.title: One litre of petrol
screens.ask: A car burns a litre of petrol. Can that same petrol be used again?
opts: Yes, it comes back next year
screens.after: Once burned, petrol is gone. Oil, gas and coal took millions of years to form. They are non-renewable.

en.text: Opal comes from the Greek word "Opallios", to see a change of colour. It is a form of silica with 3–20% water. Ethiopian opal comes from Wollo in the Amhara region. It is found in cracks of many rocks. Today it is one of Ethiopia's main export minerals. Like other minerals, it is non-renewable.

screens.title: A colourful stone
screens.ask: Ethiopia exports a gemstone that flashes red, green and blue. Which one?
screens.after: Opal shows changing colours. Ethiopian opal comes from Wollo and is a main export mineral.

screens.title: Do you know Opal?
paras: The word opal comes from the Greek "Opallios". It means "to see a change of colour".
Opal is a hydrated form of silica, similar to quartz. It holds 3% to 20% water.
Opal was first discovered in Ethiopia in the early 1990s.
Ethiopian opal comes from Wollo, in the Amhara region of northern Ethiopia.

screens.title: Where is opal found?
paras: Opal forms at a fairly low temperature.
It can occur in cracks of almost any rock: limonite, sandstone, rhyolite, marl and basalt.
It is economically valuable. It is one of Ethiopia's main export minerals.
